claims.text: P wave — atrial depolarization Normal duration < 0.12 sec (< 3 small boxes); amplitude < 2.5 mm
claims.quote: Normal duration: < 0.12 sec (< 3 small boxes) Normal amplitude: < 2.5 mm

claims.text: Best seen in lead II (rhythm) and V1 (shape); upright in I, II, aVF and inverted in aVR in sinus rhythm
claims.quote: Best seen in: Lead II (for rhythm) and V1 (for morphology) Upright in I, II, aVF; inverted in aVR (in sinus rhythm)

claims.text: PR interval — atrial depolarization plus AV node delay Start of P to start of QRS; normal 0.12–0.20 sec (3–5 small boxes)
claims.quote: From start of P to start of QRS — atrial depolarization plus AV node delay. Normal: 0.12–0.20 sec (3–5 small boxes)

claims.text: Short → pre-excitation (e.g., WPW); long → first-degree AV block
claims.quote: Short → pre-excitation (e.g., WPW) Long → first-degree AV block

claims.text: QRS complex — ventricular depolarization Normal < 0.12 sec (< 3 small boxes); narrow = supraventricular; wide suggests ventricular origin or aberrant conduction
claims.quote: Normal duration: < 0.12 sec (< 3 small boxes); narrow complexes are supraventricular in origin, wide complexes suggest ventricular origin or aberrant conduction.

claims.text: Q = first negative deflection; R = first positive deflection; S = negative deflection after the R
claims.quote: Q wave: first negative deflection R wave: first positive deflection S wave: negative deflection following R

claims.text: R-wave progression: R > S by V3–V4
claims.quote: R-wave progression R > S by V3–V4

claims.text: ST segment J point (end of QRS) to start of T; should be isoelectric. Elevation or depression → ischemia, injury, pericarditis, early repolarization or LV strain
claims.quote: End of QRS (J point) to start of T wave. Should be isoelectric. Elevation or depression can indicate ischemia, injury, pericarditis, early repolarization, or LV strain.

claims.text: T wave — ventricular repolarization Upright in I, II, V3–V6; inverted in aVR; variable in III, aVL, V1–V2
claims.quote: Usually upright in I, II, V3–V6 Inverted in aVR Variable in III, aVL, V1–V2

claims.text: Tall, peaked → hyperkalemia or hyperacute ischemia; inverted → ischemia, strain, CNS events
claims.quote: Tall, peaked T waves → hyperkalemia or hyperacute ischemia Inverted T waves → ischemia, strain, CNS events

claims.text: QT interval — total ventricular depolarization plus repolarization Start of QRS to end of T; correct for rate with Bazett: QTc = QT / √RR
claims.quote: From start of QRS to end of T. Reflects total ventricular depolarization plus repolarization. Must be corrected for rate (QTc) using Bazett's formula: QTc = QT / √ RR.

claims.text: Normal QTc < 440 ms (men), < 460 ms (women); > 500 ms = significant torsades risk
claims.quote: Normal QTc: < 440 ms (men), < 460 ms (women) Prolonged QTc > 500 ms: significant risk of torsades de pointes

claims.text: Measure in lead II or V5, where the T wave is most distinct
claims.quote: Measure in lead II or V5, ideally where T waves are most distinct

claims.text: U wave Small deflection after the T; prominent U waves → hypokalemia, bradycardia or drug effect
claims.quote: Small deflection after T. Prominent U waves suggest hypokalemia, bradycardia, or drug effect.
